feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital platform leadership and credible progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows scope well, but impact would be stronger with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter structure, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: the progression from coordinator to director is credible and supports the “systems leader” positioning.  
- Strong domain relevance: public-sector digital strategy, Drupal modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia, and AI search are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools add credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, conversion, or cost/time savings.  
- Simplify and de-duplicate: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve scanability and reduce repetition.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” and “member-facing” are consistent, but “AI-enabled”/“AI Hybrid Search” capitalization varies; “French (A2/Learning)” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)”; footer project formatting reads more like portfolio copy than CV content.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector relevance. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it should be tighter and more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace the current intro with: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for public-sector and mission-driven organizations. Combines digital strategy, governance, analytics, editorial operations, and multimedia production to build scalable, user-centered platforms and AI-enabled content experiences.”
- Tighten the list of capabilities to 4–5 themes max; the current version reads like a skills section.
- Use “has led” or “specializes in” if you want a less abrupt tone than the sentence fragment “Leads…”
- Keep “public-sector” and “AI-enabled” because they are differentiators, but avoid stacking too many nouns in one sentence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “platforms,” “governance,” and “content operations” repeat ideas already covered in the subtitle and core competencies.
- “Multimedia production” is already well established in work experience and skills, so it may not need equal prominence here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and use parallel phrasing; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial systems & workflow automation • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Multi-channel communications & advocacy operations • AI-enabled search, platform integration & content experiences • Multimedia production, livestreaming & event delivery
- Consider replacing “communications operations” with “communications leadership” if targeting director-level roles.
- Keep the most distinctive strengths first: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, AI-enabled search.
- Standardize style: use either all noun phrases or all “X & Y” constructions for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance & editorial systems,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” repeat language already used in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Use parallel, shorter project descriptions: “Built/Developed [project] that [what it did] for [audience/outcome].”
- Replace vague phrases like “improve discovery” and “continued campaign growth” with specific value, scale, or audience where possible.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled” consistently, spell out “10 x 20-foot,” and keep punctuation/structure uniform across all four entries.
- Consider trimming technical detail in the footer and emphasizing distinct project outcomes, since Drupal, workflows, and video production already appear elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI Hybrid Search” overlaps with the current freelance role; keep the footer version more outcome-focused, not process-focused.
- “Advocacy Video Series” repeats points from multiple NACo roles; highlight what made this series distinctive or omit it if space is tight.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around scope, outcomes, and 2–3 signature contributions so it feels distinct from your NACo leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused bullet: “Built cross-functional publishing workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-oriented: mention scale, speed, usability, campaign launches, or reduced publishing friction if you can quantify them.
- Recast the AI work as a flagship achievement: “Spearheading an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX for member-facing content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “digital strategy” repeat language already used heavily in NACo roles.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation/technical troubleshooting” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to business impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/organizational scope, and achievements that are distinct from your earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine channel oversight into one impact-focused bullet and add results if available: email engagement growth, social growth, campaign performance, or production volume.
- Rewrite website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make operations bullets outcome-based: specify reporting speed, decision-making improvements, reduced publishing bottlenecks, stronger compliance, or increased in-house production capacity from the studio launch.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version more strategic and outcome-focused.
- Video/programming language may duplicate earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling institutional capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps with both the later NACo director role and the earlier digital media role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, leading editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten and combine overlapping workflow bullets: “Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving publishing consistency and cross-team alignment.”
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add newsletter open/click rates, subscriber growth, video cadence, views, or turnaround-time improvements.
- Suggested version: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, leading editorial execution for advocacy and member communications. Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders. Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel. Coordinated editorial planning and improved publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications across web, email, social media and video” repeats heavily from the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this item by focusing on scaling/ownership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is broad and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and the most current strengths shown in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & discovery
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “platform modernization,” which better reflects 2022–present experience.
- Keep wording parallel: use noun phrases only, avoid mixing broad concepts with softer descriptors.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable outcomes for experience bullets rather than this skills block.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a senior-level summary. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section, so this version should emphasize platform leadership and execution themes over exhaustive tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages administration; CMS modernization; front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery); API integrations; workflow automation; Airtable-based systems; AI-enabled search.”
- Put strongest/recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API integrations.
- Tighten wording: change “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” to “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery).”
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “enterprise web platforms” or “large public-facing sites” to align with recent Drupal modernization work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating every platform/tool in both places.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with “Automation & Workflow Systems.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns with the most recent NACo leadership work, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tighten it to emphasize analysis-to-decision impact and reduce overlap with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Digital analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Replace the current line with: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI and BigQuery • KPI framework design • executive/leadership dashboards • web performance, SEO and user-behavior analysis”
- Use “executive dashboards” or “decision-ready reporting” instead of “leadership reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add one measurable signal in experience bullets tied to this skill set (e.g. reporting for 3.5M annual page views, 10,000+ page migration, or 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader “web improvement” and analytics bullets in recent roles; keep this item concise.
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical wording here.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production leadership and higher-value capabilities rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Live Events**

- Broadcast-quality video production & editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and studio system operation
- Virtual event delivery and technical coordination

- Keep this section skill-focused; let work experience carry outcomes like studio buildout, recurring programming, and advocacy/event impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in NACo roles, so avoid repeating full phrases elsewhere.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and currently duplicates the “Topline Skills” section almost exactly. This item should either add nuance or be tightened to avoid repeating the same information.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize platform administration, e.g. **CMS & Web Platforms:** Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Order by strongest/recentest relevance: keep **Drupal first** given the NACo migration and current consulting work
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless you can point to meaningful professional use; it reads lighter than the others

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly redundant with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**, which already lists the same platforms
- To reduce repetition, either keep the fuller Topline Skills version and shorten this item, or use this item only for named platforms while leaving modernization/technical context elsewhere

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and tailored to tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If space allows, group by function for readability: **Front-end:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • **Implementation:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager • **Deployment/automation:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If these were used materially in recent work, consider adding a brief qualifier elsewhere in the CV such as “front-end implementation, deployment automation, and lightweight edge scripting” rather than listing tools only.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Technical Execution” and “Technical Implementation” are semantically overlapping; consider consolidating to avoid repetition.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills. It would be stronger if grouped by function and limited to the platforms most relevant to recent workflow/system-building work.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and prioritize: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming to better signal value: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems”
- Group by purpose for readability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If space allows elsewhere, add a brief qualifier tied to impact, e.g. “used to build editorial planning, approvals, and cross-team communication workflows”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis here.
- Basecamp and Trello look less central given recent roles and can likely be dropped unless they were materially important.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this line should emphasize platform specificity and engagement-system breadth rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one higher-value capability layer instead of just tools: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter operations • audience segmentation • campaign automation**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was minor or older, consider dropping it to keep the section sharp.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “email newsletters” or “audience growth” here; those are already covered in NACo experience entries.
- If Dynamics 365 was central in the current consulting role, consider reflecting that in the recent job bullet instead of overloading this skills line.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item currently duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly. In Technical + IT, it should read more like a concise tools/methods list and avoid broad terms already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **technical SEO** to make the skill more concrete and tool-oriented.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI reporting** or **executive dashboards** for clearer business value.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced capabilities from recent roles: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this one strictly tool-based.
- “A/B testing” is fine only if you can support it with examples elsewhere; otherwise it may feel less substantiated than the rest.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content execution, and any scale/results you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size/traffic, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with concrete actions/results.
- Example: “Supported NACo’s first in-house digital team after promotion across two roles; helped execute a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and streamlined day-to-day publishing across web, email, social and multimedia while informally guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this entry more execution-focused.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable first-podcast achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim generic “contributed to” language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer scope: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add 1 measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audiences served, internal teams supported, or types/volume of research projects.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression into digital leadership remains clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/media here; the podcast launch is the unique differentiator.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and align with the stronger multimedia leadership already shown elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape as tools only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
